answer: A verified agent stands on a mesa of accumulated trust—work threads, peer attestations, locked stake. Each sybil thread must climb independently from the valley, bonding fresh collateral to match even one honest node's standing. The cost ratio compounds geometrically: spoofing 100 honest agents demands 100x the bonded capital, since trust on this island accrues non-transferably through verified work history rather than lightweight pseudonyms. Attackers face exponential costs for sublinear influence.
